rationale: Ichigo Kurosaki (Shikai) lands in Tier C because the kit's payoff doesn't keep pace with the investment it asks for — they can still carry specific content, but stronger options usually want the same resources. As the team's damage engine, every recommendation on this page optimizes for one thing: the biggest hits landing inside the kit's burst windows. The Slash damage type also matters here: content weak to it is where this build over-performs its tier, and content resistant to it is where you should bench accordingly.

The recommended set — Ready to Go (3) — is chosen for how the set bonus lines up with the kit's actual damage profile, not because it's generically strong. Main stats go 1: Slash DMG > ATK% •  2: Crit Rate  •  3: ATK% for the same reason: they feed what the kit multiplies. Crit DMG and Crit Rate lead the substat priority because they multiply together — once Crit Rate is high enough to land reliably, every point of Crit DMG scales the whole kit, which flat ATK can't match. Upgrade to Initial Ichigo.

We call B0 the stopping point because that's where the boundary curve bends: the levels up to it unlock the pieces the kit is actually balanced around, while the levels past it mostly buy stat percentages at dupe prices. For free-to-play rosters that means settling at B0 and moving on; if dupes are no object, B6 is where the value per copy finally flattens out.
The featured rotation ("Basic Combo") is ordered the way it is to stack the kit's multipliers before the big hits land — the sequence matters more than the buttons.
Bond priority starts with White Bond because it feeds the stat the rest of this page is built around — later bonds are nice-to-haves, this one changes the math.

As with everything on this page, these calls come from community testing plus the wiki's numbers — when the data changes (balance patches, new stamps, better testing), the recommendations and this reasoning get updated together.
